content.title: About
content.content: Soft oatmeal cookies with raisins are a tender treat made from whole oat flakes, wheat flour, sugar, butter, and dried raisins. The cookies have a gentle sweetness, the aroma of oats and raisins, and a soft texture that appeals to all ages.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are considered one of the most nutritious grains and are often used in baking to boost fiber content.
Raisins not only add sweetness but also provide natural antioxidants and minerals.
Soft oatmeal cookies are frequently used in children's diets because they are easy to chew and swallow.
The tradition of adding raisins to baked goods dates back to ancient Roman recipes where raisins served as a natural sweetener.
The cookies can be made gluten‑free by substituting wheat flour with gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Oats contain soluble and insoluble fiber that supports digestive health and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The cookies provide thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, which are involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Raisins are a good source of iron, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Phenolic compounds from oats and raisins help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Beta‑glucans from oats can help lower blood cholesterol levels.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional cookies contain wheat flour, which may be problematic for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Raisins and added sugar increase the calorie count; individuals monitoring blood sugar should consume the cookies in moderation.

items.title: Choking hazard for young children
items.content: Soft cookies can break into larger pieces, so they should be offered to small children under supervision.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookies as a standalone snack, crumble them into yogurt, ice cream, or use them as a base for dessert parfaits. They pair well with milk, tea, or coffee.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to maintain softness and prevent drying out.
